newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fed to tighten in Q4 amid wage pressures - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Fed to tighten in Q4 amid wage pressures - Merrill.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy modestly in the fourth quarter of this year to stave off inflationary pressure in the labour sector, Merrill Lynch chief economist Donald Straszheim said on Monday.

"There are the first signs of wage inflation already developing, and that is likely to be the reason behind the next stock market decline and the next hike in rates," Straszheim told reporters at a Merrill Lynch global issuer and investor conference in Hong Kong.
Straszheim said he expects the Fed to raise the federal funds rate modestly to 5.50 percent from the current 5.25 percent in the fourth quarter to ease wage pressures.
Price pressures have thus far been absent in the product market because improvements in technology have improved inventory management, Straszheim said.
Straszheim predicted the U.S. economy will grow at a 2.0-2.5 percent clip in 1997, with consumer prices advancing 2.5-3.0 percent.
World economies generally will enjoy the lowest inflation in years in 1997 while growth continues, he said.
"I think inflation around the world will be lower in 1997 then in any time since the mid-1960s," said Straszheim.
Inflation should average around four percent worldwide, he said.
World economic growth is likely to be stronger than in 1996, which in turn was more robust than in 1995, he said.
"So the inflation rate is falling and the growth rate is rising, which is why many markets worldwide have been doing so well," said Straszheim.
Interest rates in the United States will remain high relative to those of its major trading partners, which will contribute to a further strengthening of the U.S. dollar, he said.
"We believe the dollar will continue to rise despite the G7 meeting in Berlin two weeks ago at which the ministers said that the dollar had risen too much," said Straszheim.
By this time next year, the dollar should reach 130 yen and 1.80 marks, he predicted.
